reading.body:
itQ Data Center is an OpenStreetMap record in Wrocław, Poland, with a name that signals IT services but no confirmed capacity, operator, or ownership.

The record carries a facility name, a city, coordinates, and a website address, and nothing else. Its power figure is zero megawatts, which here means no capacity was recorded rather than a measured zero. The research note states plainly that the operator website could not be checked because search quota ran out, so the entry is filed as a plausible small data center pending further work.

Wrocław is a real technology and outsourcing hub, and a data center there would sit close to the demand it serves, about seven miles from the city's airport. That is context for why such a facility would exist. It is not evidence about this one.

For AI scaling, the useful fact is what is missing. A data center's relevance to compute depends on its power draw, its cooling, and its connectivity, and none of those appear here. A name and a coordinate do not tell you whether a building hosts racks or an office.
